title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is preparing a combinatorial description of the projective line minus three points, P^1 - {0,1,inf}, together with its S_3 = Aut(J) symmetry (J a 3-element set). The next page sets up Sigma_J = P(V(J)) with V(J) = ker(O^J -> O, sum). The marked points ('trous') are R_i, the fixed points of transpositions are Q_i (-1, 1/2, 2), and the fixed points of 3-cycles are P_omega (the primitive 6th roots of unity, with zeta = exp(2 i pi/3) introduced).

Top diagram, read in modern terms:
- pi is the (profinite or discrete) fundamental group of P^1 - {0,1,inf}.
- E_0 is a pi-set: probably the cusps (or tangential base points) of the universal cover lying over the marked points, so that pi_0(E_0) = E_0/pi is the set of the three cusps.
- The vertical map E_0 -> Ssgr(pi) sends a lift to its stabiliser, i.e. its inertia subgroup. Ssgr means the set of subgroups. The map is pi-equivariant, so it descends to pi_0(E_0) -> Ssgr(pi)/pi (conjugacy classes of inertia subgroups).
- He then enlarges pi to Sigma, an extension 1 -> pi -> Sigma -> Gamma -> 1 with Sigma/pi = Gamma and Sigma = Gamma.pi. Here Gamma is the symmetry group (S_3, or a subgroup) acting on the curve. Sigma is then the fundamental group of the quotient orbifold/stack [ (P^1 - {0,1,inf}) / Gamma ].
- Sigma acts on E_0 and on Ssgr(pi) compatibly, so the inertia data become Sigma-equivariant.

The sphere drawings make this concrete:
- The equator is the real circle through 0, 1, inf, with small loops around each point (R_0, R_inf, ...).
- The poles xi, xi' are the order-3 points.
- Paths are labelled a_i^±, b_i^±, c_i, d_i, with composites such as d_i^+(c_i^+)^{-1}; these are generators and connecting paths used to write down the extension.
- The right-hand sketches track how points map under a quotient (inf -> inf', 0'; 0 -> 1'; ...).
- The bottom sketches carry the instruction 'définir D ...', meaning define a domain D or a set of paths with data (a_i, R_i), (inf', 0).

Purpose: an explicit presentation of the semidirect-type extension of S_3 by pi_1(P^1 - {0,1,inf}), with its inertia and torsion data. This is the genus-0 building block needed for the Galois action on the Teichmüller tower and for the relations of order 2 and 3.
errors: No mathematical errors are detectable. The page is a set of working sketches with no claims.
The top diagram is partly crossed out ("Ssgr C"), and the target 'Ssgr(E)/pi' looks inconsistent with the later 'Ssgr(pi)/pi'. It is probably a slip or a first attempt.

ideas.what: Equivariant map from the set of cusps (lifts) to subgroups via stabilisers, giving inertia conjugacy classes indexed by pi_0(E_0) = E_0/pi
ideas.modern_name: inertia subgroups / cuspidal decomposition data of a profinite (orbifold) fundamental group
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Grothendieck SGA1; Ihara, Nakamura in the anabelian context)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (tame fundamental group, inertia); Esquisse d'un programme (discrete/profinite tower)

ideas.what: Extension 1 -> pi -> Sigma -> Gamma -> 1 of the symmetry group of P^1 - {0,1,inf} by its fundamental group, with Sigma the fundamental group of the quotient stack
ideas.modern_name: orbifold fundamental group of [M_{0,4}/S_3]; S_3-extension used in the definition of GT
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; Grothendieck (Esquisse) for the general programme
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (role of automorphism groups of order 2 and 3 in genus 0 and 1)

ideas.what: Drawn sphere with S_3-symmetric cell structure: the real circle through 0, 1, inf, the order-3 points at the poles, and named paths and loops
ideas.modern_name: explicit generators for pi_1 of P^1 minus three points; tangential base points; dessin-like cell decomposition

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard working sketches for the S_3-equivariant presentation of pi_1(P^1 - {0,1,inf}) and its inertia. The content is well covered by the Esquisse and by later GT/anabelian literature (Drinfeld, Ihara, Nakamura, Schneps). Nothing finished or novel is visible.
transcription_corrections: The phrase read as 'Sigma opérations [?] ci-dessus' is very uncertain. It looks more like 'E opposé (?) ci-dessus' attached to the brace under 'Ssgr(pi) -> Ssgr(E)/pi'.
The labels at the north and south poles of the first sphere are a xi-like symbol (xi, with a bar), not 'zeta'.
Bottom row: 'pi —— E_0 ——> Ssgr(pi)/pi', with Sigma ⊃ pi indicated by the vertical 'U' symbol (pi a subgroup of Sigma).

The upside-down marginal notes are rotated text. The lower ones read roughly 'définir D + ... (inf', 0)' and 'définir D ... (a_i, R_i)'. The right one is a correspondence list 'inf -> inf', 0'; 0 -> 1'; 1 -> ...'.
